chapter: Hollywood and the break with Thornhill
title: 'Down the Old Ox Road' and 'Spring Is Here' as Claude's song choices
summary: The college crowd loved 'Old Ox Road'; Claude brought songs hot off the press such as the Rodgers tune.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You were telling me just now off tape the significance of the phrase, 'down the old ox road.'
Yes.
Maybe it's because I'm not U.S. born.
Yes, right.
You described it was popular with the college crowd.
Right. 'Down The Old

Ox Road" was very popular among the college group. I think the "Old Ox Road" is what would be considered lovers lane, you know. The guys would go out and ... But it may have appeared in a -- may have been in a picture! I don't know. The first rendition of it I heard, or maybe at the same time, was Bing Crosby made a recording of "Down The Old Ox Road."

But I didn't know when I was singing at the club, that -- it got a big hand from the college group. I didn't even understand why it took me time to figure out why it was so popular. But It's a college song. And "L'amour Toujours L'amour", I guess -- we're still trying to keep to the traditional -- you know, give them a little swing treatment to some better classics -- if you want to call "L'amour Toujours L'amour" a classic. You know, it's a -- what?
Wasn't that a Tin Pan Alley song?
I don't think so. I think it's a -- I don't even know who wrote it.

I guess the impression I got were those who, perhaps, modeled on some --
No, no. It was an art song something in the category of the kind of stuff that maybe Rudolf Friml --
Yeah, light operetta.
Yes. And, of course, 'Spring Is Here' --
Well for me, that's the pick of the bunch.
Yeah, that's a beautiful tune. I don't know if that was written for a picture or what.
Since Claude suggested most of these songs and brought on the music and arrangements, he probably knew why we should do it.
Richard Rogers is the composer of that song. Isn't he?
Yes.
He wrote it in 1938.
I just looked in my copy of Alec Wilder, and I see it was written for a show in 1938 called,
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
"I Married An Angel."
Oh yes.
You remember that?

Yes, I remember it now. But I didn't see the picture, and I never heard any other version of (inaudible). I guess -- we probably got it. Claude would've been able to get any music before anybody else did.
In fact, getting back to "Gone With The Wind," "Gone With The Wind" was written in anticipation of it having been used in the movie Gone With The Wind, but it wasn't.
So, Claude knew these things. I didn't particularly know or, couldn't have cared less. It was just something to sing.
And that was a very inspired choice, I would say.
Yes, it was beautiful.
Your song was hot off the press.
Um hum!
